callout.title: Buy evidence that removes a specific collection obstacle
callout.body: Experienced recovery operators spend against documented impediments rather than treating every visible property record as a payable lead.
items: Before buying certified corporate records, ask the treasury which merger, dissolution, or officer-authority documents the specific claim requires.
Start with corporate claims above $25,000, but quarantine records whose displayed amount is only a category or estimate until value is confirmed.
Ask the issuing municipality whether an uncashed warrant remains payable there or has transferred to the state before preparing either claim packet.
Batch evidence purchases by confirmed claimant and jurisdiction; stop buying records when ownership continuity cannot be established.

sections.heading: 2. Assemble twelve narrow layers without twelve paid subscriptions
paragraphs: Build the production stack around a case identifier that survives every export. Use a jurisdiction prefix, source property identifier, and internal sequence; keep owner names out of filenames that could appear in email previews. Python and SQLite perform record normalization and candidate scoring locally, while Airtable Free holds a limited operational queue containing case identifiers, dates, and task ownership rather than identity documents. Microsoft 365 Business Basic provides business email and controlled document storage. Choose one authoritative document repository instead of copying passports into the CRM, inbox, and contractor chat. The twelve layers below are functions, not twelve mandatory paid accounts. Several are free utilities, and the archive and OCR layers remain disabled until a concrete workload justifies them. Treat every stated price as an exact planning input for the named tier, not a verified current offer. Confirm checkout pricing, billing commitment, taxes, regional availability, and contractual data terms before purchase. Model annual commitments as cash obligations even when a vendor advertises a monthly equivalent. No paid tool should become a prerequisite for inspecting a public ledger, calculating a lawful fee, or telling an owner how to claim directly.

Use the matrix to distinguish license arithmetic from total operating cost. One Microsoft seat at $6 per month, one Bitwarden Teams seat at $4, and one Backblaze Computer Backup subscription at $9 produce a $19 monthly-equivalent software baseline under the listed assumptions. Add a $15 Dropbox Sign Essentials seat only after confirming the receiving agency accepts the resulting execution method. The baseline then becomes $34, before domain registration, taxes, transaction charges, or optional usage. Microsoft and Bitwarden annual billing alone implies $120 of yearly license commitment for one seat each; budget the actual payment schedule rather than assuming monthly cancellation. For optional Amazon S3 storage, 100 GB at $0.023 per GB-month creates $2.30 of storage charges before requests and transfer. For Amazon Textract Detect Document Text, 1,000 pages at $0.0015 per page creates $1.50 of processing charges under the stated regional tier. These calculations are procurement assumptions, not the whole $1,500–$8,000 operating envelope. Most spending belongs to people, evidence, owner acquisition, insurance, and administration. Add contractor licenses only when access is necessary, and remove those accounts when the assignment ends.

Automation should produce reviewable evidence, not impersonate the claimant or assert ownership. Store each downloaded ledger with source URL, retrieval timestamp, permitted-use notes, and a SHA-256 digest. Preserve source spelling alongside normalized names so punctuation cleanup cannot erase an important distinction. A SQLite uniqueness constraint on jurisdiction and property identifier prevents duplicate outreach; a separate ownership table records the Secretary of State entity number and evidence supporting each link. GitHub Free stores code and synthetic test fixtures only, never live claimant documents or credentials. Require multifactor authentication on business accounts, encrypt workstations, and restrict contractor access to assigned folders. Test a backup restoration before trusting a successful upload indicator. If OCR fails on a warrant image, compare the original manually instead of allowing the extracted amount to drive a fee quote. If a portal lacks an authorized automation route, use scheduled manual checks rather than bypassing access controls or flooding endpoints. Maintain a documented retention schedule that reconciles agency requirements, contractual needs, disputes, and applicable privacy duties. Cheap infrastructure remains useful only when an operator can explain where each fact originated and who changed it.

sections.heading: 3. Underwrite the recovery play before scaling record matching
paragraphs: The priority implementation is unclaimed_property_escheatment_arbitrage, the TRACK_1 State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery play. Ingest permitted state controller or treasury ledgers and uncashed municipal or corporate warrant registries, prioritizing amounts above $25,000. Separate a warrant still payable by its issuer from property already held by a state treasury; the correct obligor determines the evidence route. Cross-match corporate officers through Secretary of State filings, then establish entity continuity through name changes, mergers, dissolutions, and assignments. An officer-name match creates a research lead, not authority to sign a recovery agreement. The play's commercial fee range is 10–25%, but that range never overrides state law. California Code of Civil Procedure §1582 supplies agreement requirements and a 10% ceiling for covered recovery agreements; Texas Property Code §74.507 also controls covered recovery assistance agreements and limits compensation. Read each provision's scope and timing before configuring intake. Store the governing jurisdiction, eligible signing date, maximum permitted compensation, required disclosures, and reviewer in the case record. When a timing restriction is unresolved, defer solicitation or execution as applicable instead of relabeling the fee as research.

Use a $30,000 eligible claim and a lawful 10% contingent fee as the transparent unit model. Successful recovery produces $3,000 of operator service fees and leaves $27,000 with the owner before any separately applicable owner obligations. The $30,000 principal never becomes operator revenue. Twenty such paid recoveries generate the Conservative $60,000 revenue case; eighty-five generate Base revenue of $255,000; one hundred fifty generate Scaled revenue of $450,000. These are arithmetic equivalents, not asserted throughput or conversion rates. A $100,000 claim at 10% produces $10,000 of fees, while a $30,000 claim at 25% would produce $7,500 only where that rate and agreement are lawful. Do not build the business around the higher rate without jurisdiction-specific support. For triage, suppose an eligible $3,000 fee has a 40% collection probability, $500 of remaining direct costs, and a $300 collection-delay allowance. Its planning contribution is $1,200 minus $800, or $400 before fixed overhead. Document those assumptions rather than presenting them as historical performance. Reject low-value cases when evidence costs consume expected contribution; combine records only when ownership and agency procedures genuinely support aggregation.

Customer distrust is an operating constraint, not a copywriting problem to solve with urgency. Disclose prominently that the owner can claim directly from the relevant state without paying a recovery service, provide the official claim URL, and explain the paid work actually offered. Avoid government styling, invented deadlines, or claims of exclusive access to public records. Verify a corporate contact through an independently obtained business channel before requesting identity documents. Have distributions sent directly to the verified owner whenever the agency process permits; invoice the contractual service fee separately after the agreed earning event. If a process requires custody of client money, resolve its legal, banking, and accounting requirements before accepting that workflow. Obtain an EIN through the IRS without paying a reseller merely to submit the application. Keep the entity account, reserve account, and bookkeeping ledger distinct from personal spending. California Civil Code §1798.81.5 requires reasonable security for covered personal information; translate applicable duties into restricted folders, secure transmission, vendor review, and documented deletion. Identity mismatch sends the case back to evidence review. It never becomes an invitation to submit a more persuasive but unsupported ownership narrative.

sections.heading: 4. Prove one complete claim workflow before increasing overhead
paragraphs: Pre-launch readiness means a complete evidence trail can survive handoff, correction, and recovery from failure. Select one jurisdiction, one corporate claimant profile, and a small permitted sample of public records. Run the intake through deduplication, ownership review, statutory configuration, outreach drafting, agreement preparation, evidence indexing, and claim-status tracking. Use synthetic identity documents during rehearsal and do not submit a fictional claim to an agency. Confirm that every agreement states the correct fee basis, treats timing restrictions correctly, and explains the owner's direct claim option. Recalculate the fee independently of the template so a stale percentage cannot silently survive. Have the evidence contractor explain the corporate ownership chain to the principal operator without access to unrelated cases. Then restore the rehearsal folder from backup and compare its inventory with the original. Record missing permissions, broken links, incomplete signatures, and ambiguous amount fields as defects with an assigned owner. No claim enters production merely because the CRM shows a green status. Readiness is the ability to reconstruct the entire case from source records without relying on someone's memory or an undocumented conversation with the claimant.

Install a thirteen-week cash forecast before signing recurring contracts. Separate beginning cash, collected fees, fixed payments, case-variable payments, taxes reserved from actual activity, and ending unrestricted cash. Keep prospective recoveries in a separate schedule until the contractual earning and collection conditions are satisfied. A state acknowledging a claim does not establish that the operator's invoice is earned or paid. At the $1,500 fixed-overhead planning level, one useful monthly allocation is $120 for software and connectivity, $500 for scheduled support, $250 for evidence and delivery, $200 for outreach, $180 for insurance and administration, and $250 for contingency. These six amounts total $1,500; replace them with actual quotes and avoid charging the same expense again to a variable-cost line. During each weekly review, compare committed obligations with reserve cash and the next eight weeks of unavoidable payments. If the cash floor is threatened, pause discretionary evidence purchases, reduce outreach, and defer additional jurisdictions before missing essential security or filing obligations. Owner distributions follow funded operating needs, not the headline amount of a newly discovered property. A promising claim remains illiquid until the relevant cash actually arrives.

Expand only after measuring the bottleneck with paid-case data. Track eligible records reviewed, confirmed ownership matches, owner responses, signed lawful agreements, complete submissions, agency deficiency requests, recoveries, earned fees, and cash receipts as separate events. Record elapsed days between events instead of collapsing them into one conversion percentage. A high deficiency rate calls for better evidence preparation, not additional prospect volume. A low response rate calls for verified contacts and clearer direct-claim disclosure, not escalating pressure. The first two scorecard cases retain 1 FT + 2 C: the principal controls economics and claimant relationships while narrowly scoped contractors support research and document preparation. The Scaled case permits 2 FT + 3 C, but additional access follows demonstrated workload and documented responsibilities. Require confidentiality terms, least-privilege access, and deletion confirmation when assignments end. Expand matching automation only after a reviewed sample demonstrates acceptable false-positive handling. Expand claim-status tracking through permitted interfaces or disciplined reminders, not unattended assumptions about agency progress. chapters.question_prompt: What kills 80% of newcomers in unclaimed property recovery, and what forensic metrics detect margin leaks, regulatory landmines, or platform bans before they wipe out capital?

chapters.subtitle: Treasury Identity Defects, Finder-Fee Restrictions, Claim Reversals, Portal Suspensions & Cohort-Level Cash Controls
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #5, Unclaimed Property Recovery, holds Rank #04 with an 89/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, but strong economics require disciplined rejection of defective claims. Within the volume's 12 mapped plays, this chapter separates treasury recovery from adjacent freight-audit contingencies and identifies where identity errors, invalid agreements, duplicate submissions, portal abuse, and premature fee recognition destroy cash. The canonical annual owner profit cases are $15,000 Conservative, $95,625 Base, and $225,000 Scaled; client property is never operator revenue. Use claim-level evidence chains, state-specific contract checks, cohort contribution tests, and explicit stop conditions to protect those outcomes. The question's 80% figure is a framing device, not an established industry failure statistic.

sections.heading: 1. Reject defective ownership before purchasing another lead
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is treating a treasury search result as a receivable. A matching surname, historical address, or employer proves only that further research may be worthwhile; it does not establish entitlement. Separate discovery, identity corroboration, authority, submission, adjudication, payment, and fee collection into distinct claim states. Record the state property identifier, holder name, reported owner, property category, source timestamp, and evidence supporting each transition. Never merge two records solely because a matching algorithm assigns a high similarity score. For an individual, compare historical addresses and name changes against documents the treasury actually accepts. For a corporation, reconcile the reported entity with Secretary of State records, merger documents, and the authorized signer's capacity. A dissolved subsidiary and its parent are not interchangeable claimants. For an estate, identify the lawful representative rather than assuming the nearest relative can sign. Use a protected evidence repository with restricted access, not attachments scattered across contractor inboxes. Airtable can hold operational identifiers while the sensitive documents remain in a separately controlled workspace. Stop intake when identity conflicts remain unresolved; paying for more outreach only compounds the cost of an unusable claim and exposes another person's records.

The second cluster of traps is economic: buying stale lists, chasing tiny balances, counting duplicate properties twice, and paying contractors for submissions rather than accepted evidence. A listing with an undisclosed balance cannot support a precise fee forecast; price the research exposure separately until the amount is established. Consider an illustrative $600 property with a permissible 10% fee: maximum gross service revenue is $60. Thirty minutes of research at a $30 hourly loaded rate costs $15, and another hour of document handling costs $30, leaving $15 before acquisition, software, rejection risk, and collection work. That claim becomes destructive after one avoidable rework cycle. By contrast, several verified properties belonging to one owner may share an evidence package, but only where the receiving agencies accept the same documents. Deduplicate using jurisdiction plus property identifier, then link related claims without deleting their separate status histories. Compensate researchers for verified ownership packages with documented quality checks rather than raw lead counts. Establish a maximum research spend per unqualified lead and require an explicit reason before exceeding it. A large public balance attached to the wrong entity is less valuable than a modest balance with clean authority and an economical evidence path.

Customer distrust is a unit-economics problem, not merely a branding problem. The third cluster of traps includes treasury impersonation, artificial urgency, concealing the free direct-claim route, and collecting identity documents before explaining who operates the service. Use your actual business identity, describe the source of the property lead, disclose that the owner can claim directly without hiring you, and provide the official treasury address independently of your engagement link. Never imply a government affiliation or invent an expiration deadline. These shortcuts increase complaints, payment disputes, and the chance that legitimate outreach infrastructure becomes unusable. Separate permission to communicate from authority to submit a claim; a reply to an email is not a signed engagement or an agency authorization. If commercial email is used, implement the sender identification and opt-out requirements of 15 U.S.C. § 7704 where applicable. Evaluate telephone and text outreach under the applicable calling rules before enabling automated campaigns. Track complaints by lead supplier, message version, and channel rather than averaging them across the business. One substantiated impersonation complaint triggers an immediate pause of the implicated template while evidence is preserved. The remedy is a corrected process, not another sending domain.

callout.body: Experienced operators reduce repeated work while preserving a separate entitlement trail for every property.

sections.heading: 2. Engineer around invalid agreements, reversals, and restricted access
paragraphs: Finder economics are jurisdiction-specific, and a contract template is not a portable operating license. California Code of Civil Procedure § 1582 addresses agreement timing, compensation restrictions, and required agreement content; its 10% limit must be read with the section's timing and applicability rules. Texas Property Code § 74.507 governs agreements to recover reported property, including a 10% compensation ceiling and enforceability requirements. New York Abandoned Property Law § 1416 provides a separate framework for recovery agreements. Do not infer identical clocks, covered parties, exemptions, or signature requirements from similar percentages. Before solicitation or signing, record the governing program, property status, reporting or delivery dates needed by that statute, finder registration requirements, permitted compensation, required disclosures, and allowed representative activity. Where a date determines whether an agreement is valid, obtain that date from an authoritative record rather than substituting the day your researcher found the listing. A claim can be genuine while the fee agreement is invalid. When requirements cannot be satisfied, pause the paid engagement and give the owner the direct-claim route; do not relabel the same recovery fee as research, processing, or consulting to evade a restriction. Version every state-specific agreement against its effective legal requirements.

A clawback is not one event. Distinguish an agency's recovery of an erroneous property payment, a customer's demand to reverse an unearned fee, a card chargeback, and an accounting credit issued after a service dispute. Each requires different evidence and a different ledger entry. Approval notices may precede disbursement, and a deposited payment may later become disputed when ownership evidence proves defective. Define the fee-earning event, payer, payment route, dispute procedure, and refund treatment in the valid agreement. Prefer treasury payment directly to the rightful owner with a separately documented service invoice where the program permits that arrangement. Do not route client property through the operating account merely to make collection easier. Custody changes the operational and legal analysis and must be evaluated before implementation. An illustrative $10,000 owner recovery at a permissible 10% fee creates $1,000 of service consideration, not $10,000 of operator revenue. If a $300 portion is later refunded, the ledger must reflect that reversal rather than burying it as miscellaneous spending. Preserve the agreement version, entitlement evidence, agency correspondence, payment confirmation, and invoice together. A refund reserve based on observed dispute cohorts supports liquidity planning but does not automatically replace the applicable revenue-recognition policy.

Access failures often begin as productivity experiments: scripted logins against portal restrictions, bulk harvesting beyond published permissions, shared claimant credentials, forged authorization, and repeated submissions under alternate identities. These shortcuts can trigger suspension, termination, or a permanent ban under the applicable service terms, while deception and unauthorized access create additional exposure. Treat a CAPTCHA, authentication challenge, or explicit rate limit as a boundary, not an engineering puzzle to bypass. Use published downloads, permitted interfaces, and agency-approved representative workflows. Read-only access reduces mutation risk but does not authorize collecting every record visible to an account. Keep a source register with permitted uses, rate limits, credential owner, and revocation procedure. Use individual accounts where supported and store secrets in a controlled password manager such as 1Password Business rather than a spreadsheet. Restrict contractors to assigned cases, redact irrelevant identifiers, and remove access when assignments end. One exposed identity document triggers containment, access review, and assessment of applicable notification duties; it is not merely another service ticket. Measure authentication errors and access-denial responses separately from ordinary empty search results. When an interface rejects automation, stop the affected job and switch only to an expressly permitted workflow, preserving legitimate manual work elsewhere.

sections.heading: 3. Detect margin leaks with cohort contribution and liquidity telemetry
paragraphs: Anchor every dashboard to the canonical fee basis. Conservative produces $60,000 in annual recognized service fees, $45,000 in implied total costs, and $15,000 in owner net profit at 25%, with 1 FT + 2 C. Base produces $255,000 in fees, $159,375 in costs, and $95,625 in owner net profit at 37.5%, also with 1 FT + 2 C. Scaled produces $450,000 in fees, $225,000 in costs, and $225,000 in owner net profit at 50%, with 2 FT + 3 C. These costs are the arithmetic residuals of the supplied scorecard, not a newly estimated staffing budget. If every engagement hypothetically earned a lawful 10% fee, those revenues would correspond to $600,000, $2,550,000, and $4,500,000 of underlying recoveries respectively. Real fee mixes can differ, so never make that illustration a property-volume commitment. Client recoveries remain outside operator revenue. The $1,500–$8,000 monthly opex range describes an operating planning range, not a cap on all annual scenario costs. Reconcile labor, acquisition, variable fulfillment, and refunds explicitly. The 3–12 month time to first deal means that a promising pipeline can coexist with insufficient cash, particularly near the $5,000 startup-capital minimum.

Track contribution by acquisition cohort and jurisdiction rather than celebrating gross approvals. Define claim contribution as earned service fees net of reversals, less attributable acquisition, research, document procurement, submission, and collection costs. Keep shared overhead separate so the cohort measure does not masquerade as owner net profit. In an illustrative cohort of 100 purchased leads, $2,000 acquisition spending plus $3,000 research and fulfillment spending creates $5,000 of direct cost. Ten completed claims at $800 each produce $8,000 before reversals and $3,000 contribution before overhead. Two full $800 fee reversals reduce that contribution to $1,400; another $1,500 rework cycle makes it negative $100. This sensitivity explains why approval rate alone is a weak operating signal. Measure lead-to-qualified-owner conversion, qualified-to-authorized conversion, first-pass document acceptance, earned-to-collected fee conversion, and reversal dollars divided by the relevant earned-fee cohort. Preserve both counts and dollars so one large claim cannot conceal widespread defects. Use mature cohorts for conversion comparisons and label younger cohorts by age. Otherwise, an improvement in sourcing may merely reflect older claims finally paying while recent low-quality purchases have not reached adjudication. Investigate every material variance at the source-record level before changing staff targets.

Set circuit-breakers as internal management thresholds, not invented treasury standards. For a rolling sample of at least 30 reviewed packages, a first-pass deficiency rate above 15% pauses the responsible template or research source for review. Any confirmed wrong-owner submission stops the affected matching rule immediately, regardless of sample size. A reversal rate above 5% of earned fees in a mature cohort triggers a reserve review and freezes expansion of that cohort's acquisition channel. Treat these starting thresholds as hypotheses to recalibrate with observed loss severity and agency behavior. Monitor days from complete submission to payment separately from days waiting for owner documents; otherwise, staff can improve apparent speed by postponing the submission timestamp. Escalate claims aging beyond twice the comparable jurisdiction's trailing median, but check published processing updates before assuming a defect. Maintain a thirteen-week cash forecast excluding owner property, unearned fees, and speculative balances. A $12,000 unrestricted cash balance against $6,000 of monthly net cash burn provides roughly two months of runway. That is shorter than the stated first-deal window's lower end, so additional lead purchases should stop unless committed receipts or new capital close the gap. Pipeline value cannot pay current payroll.

sections.heading: 4. Keep freight contingencies separate and make automation fail safely
paragraphs: The mapped play freight_detention_audit_contingency, Automated Parcel, LTL Freight & Tariff Overcharge Contingency Auditing, belongs to TRACK_1 and is an adjacent recovery workflow, not permission to import freight fees into treasury claims. Ingest mid-market shippers' UPS, FedEx, and LTL EDI billing feeds through authorized read-only interfaces, and obtain CBP Form 7501 entry summaries through an authorized importer or broker data channel. There is no assumption that every carrier or customs document has a public API. Match invoices to contracted rates, shipment characteristics, service commitments, adjustment notices, and payment records before flagging late-delivery SLA refunds, dimensional-weight errors, duplicate charges, freight classification issues, or potential duty drawback. Carrier service guarantees may be suspended, excluded, waived, or subject to short claim deadlines. An algorithmic exception is therefore a research candidate, not a collectible receivable. At a contractual 40% contingency within the mapped 35–50% range, $20,000 in verified, collected carrier credits produces $8,000 of service fees and leaves $12,000 with the shipper. If direct audit and collection work costs $3,000, contribution is $5,000 before shared overhead and reversals. Keep this illustration outside the canonical treasury scenarios unless actual booked service fees are deliberately included and reconciled.

Duty drawback adds a distinct statutory evidence burden. Under 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and the applicable rules in 19 CFR Part 190, some qualifying drawback provisions can return up to 99% of eligible duties, taxes, and fees, but an entry summary alone does not establish eligibility. The specific provision determines the required import, export or destruction, merchandise, possession, and record evidence. Separate discovery and data preparation from activities requiring a licensed customs broker or another authorized filer under 19 U.S.C. § 1641. Never promise a customs recovery simply because duties appear on Form 7501. For illustration, $50,000 of duties fully eligible for a 99% return yields $49,500 before service compensation; a separately valid 40% contingent service agreement would yield $19,800 only on that realized recovery. Eligibility defects reduce the recovery base before the fee is calculated. If service-guarantee refunds are unavailable, apply the mapped fallback: pivot toward non-waivable dimensional-weight and duplicate-charge recoveries where governing terms support that treatment, plus LTL freight-class corrections and contract-rate benchmarking. Do not assume every billing error survives every contractual deadline. Benchmarking future rates creates prospective savings, not recovered cash, and requires a separately defined compensation basis rather than a fictional refund invoice.

The final asymmetric failure is allowing automation to convert one bad assumption into hundreds of external acts. Record matching and claim status tracking are the primary automation levers; signing, identity attestation, and submission authority require controls appropriate to the receiving program. Run matching changes against a retained set of previously adjudicated examples, including common names, deceased owners, renamed entities, and duplicate property records. Compare false-positive rates before enabling broader use. A status worker should use an idempotent event key so replaying an agency notification cannot create another invoice or submission. A portal outage should create a retry task within permitted limits, not mark every pending claim rejected. Require two-person review for changes to payment instructions and independently verify the request through an established contact channel. Keep a dated change log and a reversible deployment path for matching rules, document templates, and fee calculations. Every week, sample accepted cases as well as rejected ones; successful payment does not prove that the underlying process was sound. Expand only when mature cohort contribution, available cash, document quality, and permitted access remain intact. The small-team advantage comes from eliminating repeatable defects, not from making unverified submissions faster.

This chapter maps 12 sourcing plays, from corporate warrants and merger remnants to a separately controlled medical-recovery adjacency. Build a narrow jurisdictional lane, reconcile owner identity before outreach, explain direct claiming, and sell document coordination rather than privileged access. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $15,000 Conservative, $95,625 Base, and $225,000 Scaled; recognized revenue means service fees, never recovered principal. A measured 3–12 month acquisition program combines public-record signals, professional referrals, restrained outbound, and secure intake to target the first 3-to-10 paid wins without confusing signatures with collections.

sections.heading: 1. Mine Twelve Evidence-Rich Plays Instead of Buying Name Lists
paragraphs: Start with one state and one ownership pattern: operating companies with stale addresses, dissolved entities with documented successors, or estates with appointed representatives. Search the official treasury portal first; use MissingMoney only as a participating-state discovery layer, then return to the custodian for instructions. Public visibility does not establish permission for bulk extraction. Follow portal terms, rate limits, and published download procedures; where permitted, request a dated public-record extract rather than repeatedly querying individual names. Capture the property identifier, holder, owner spelling, reported address, asset category, amount visibility, and retrieval date. Preserve the original record alongside normalized fields. A matching engine can strip punctuation and expand business suffixes, but it must never turn a similar name into a verified claimant. Combine treasury evidence with Secretary of State filings, SEC EDGAR merger exhibits, county probate dockets, and corporate contact pages. Rank leads by recoverable fee opportunity and document accessibility, not advertised property totals. Three apparently valuable entries can represent the same ownership problem or entirely different people. The best first account usually has an active controller, a traceable historical address, and one custodian with a clear corporate claim checklist. That combination shortens evidence collection without relying on privileged access.

Use the twelve plays in the matrix as distinct sourcing hypotheses, not twelve interchangeable datasets. Corporate warrants, vendor overpayments, payroll balances, and utility deposits begin with different holders and require different proof. A city check register can reveal an uncashed warrant before treasury transfer, but the city may retain the obligation or apply a separate stale-check procedure. Determine custody before describing it as escheated property. Merger remnants, closed branches, and dissolved companies reward historical entity research; their failure mode is assuming that a familiar trade name proves succession. Estates, trust distributions, and insurance proceeds reward representative relationships, but a public docket does not authorize disclosure of sensitive beneficiary information. Securities and escrow balances introduce valuation and entitlement questions that can overwhelm a first-time operator. Prioritize cash claims with accessible records before pursuing those complications. For each ordinary recovery lane, calculate the prospective fee using a rate actually permitted for that property, jurisdiction, and agreement date. A $40,000 cash balance at an allowable 10% produces $4,000 of potential service revenue, not $40,000 of revenue. If the permitted rate is 5%, the same evidence burden must fit inside $2,000. Recalculate acquisition spend before contacting the owner.

Treat hospital_lien_medical_receivables_arbitrage as the required TRACK_1 adjacency, not a treasury-claim shortcut. Its operating name is Out-of-Network Medical Claim & ERISA Appeal Contingency Recovery. Partner with surgical centers, air/ground ambulance operators, and specialty clinics to review denied or underpaid commercial claims, but segment each service by payer, plan, facility status, and dispute eligibility. Federal No Surprises Act payment disputes are not a universal route for every out-of-network bill; ground ambulance services generally sit outside its federal balance-billing framework. For eligible disputes, track the 30-business-day open-negotiation period and ordinarily the four-business-day IDR initiation window that follows, while checking applicable extensions and current agency instructions. Automate evidence assembly and deadline reminders, not unsupported eligibility judgments. An illustrative $100,000 incremental payer recovery at a contractually permitted 25% contingency generates $25,000 in service fees; a 20–35% range yields $20,000–$35,000 before case costs. Keep this model separate from treasury finder caps and the canonical volume forecast. Execute BAAs where required, encrypt EDI transfers, and restrict access to minimum-necessary claim data. If IDR timing has lapsed, evaluate a timely ERISA administrative appeal independently; group-health adverse benefit determinations generally allow at least 180 days to appeal. An appeal is not an automatic substitute for a payment dispute.

callout.title: Find the Evidence Advantage Before the Owner Conversation
callout.body: Experienced recovery operators win with a better ownership file, a reachable representative, and a narrower promise.
items: Search historical legal names and prior addresses separately; preserve each property identifier so normalization never erases distinct owners.
Ask controllers which entity retains pre-merger records before requesting documents; a records custodian often matters more than the current executive.
Check whether a warrant remains with its issuing government before applying treasury claim instructions or quoting a finder agreement.
For medical partners, map remittance dates and appeal deadlines before estimating recoveries; expired rights are not restored by better automation.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify the Claim, Representative, and Permitted Fee Before Outreach
paragraphs: Build a qualification scorecard that separates ranking from mandatory eligibility. Award up to 30 points for ownership evidence, 20 for document accessibility, 20 for fee contribution, 15 for representative reachability, and 15 for timing clarity. An exact entity name plus a historical address can justify research, but the custodian still determines acceptable ownership proof. Require 75 points before personalized outbound and 85 before spending on complex records; these are internal starting thresholds, not measured industry benchmarks. Independently stop any case with disputed authority, an ineligible agreement date, a prohibited fee, or an unresolved identity collision. A high score cannot override those conditions. Create a state rules sheet recording finder registration, licensing, permissible contract timing, fee basis, required wording, cancellation provisions where applicable, and direct-claim disclosures. California Code of Civil Procedure section 1582, for example, makes certain agreements during the reporting-to-post-delivery interval invalid and limits finder compensation. Read the actual statutory sequence rather than assuming that an old-looking listing is immediately contractable. Record the source URL, review date, and reviewer beside each rule. If the rule depends on delivery timing that the public record omits, ask the custodian before soliciting a paid engagement.

Translate the score into a spending ceiling with explicit uncertainty. Suppose a documented $50,000 cash claim permits a 10% fee, yielding $5,000 if collected. Assume, for illustration, a 60% probability of collection after signing, $650 of expected processing labor, $150 of expected document costs, and $300 of allocated acquisition work. Expected contribution is $3,000 minus $1,100, or $1,900, before shared overhead and tax treatment. These costs must represent probability-weighted spend across successful and failed cases; using only successful-case costs overstates the result. A $4,000 claim under identical assumptions produces $240 of expected fees and loses $860. Either redesign that workflow around materially lower costs or send the owner to direct claiming. Do not conceal several small claims inside a large headline balance. Track each property separately and aggregate only where ownership, contract coverage, and custodian procedures allow it. For medical work, subtract IDR administrative and entity fees, specialist review, and unrecovered case costs under the engagement's allocation terms. A promising payer balance can still be uneconomic after eligibility screening. Apply a maximum research budget per lead and require a specific missing fact before extending it.

Design intake so that trust improves while sensitive-data exposure falls. Keep discovery records in a permissioned CRM such as HubSpot or Airtable, but store identity documents in a separately controlled repository with access logs and retention settings. Those product names do not establish suitability for health information; medical work requires the appropriate service configuration, contractual protections, and BAAs where applicable. Avoid collecting Social Security numbers during prospecting. Send a secure upload request only after the representative understands the claim, the fee, and the purpose of each document. Confirm corporate authority through custodian requirements, not merely a business email domain. For estates, distinguish the person discussing the claim from the person authorized to sign. Preserve name changes, address history, and supporting records as an evidence chain rather than silently editing the original identity. Default to payment from the custodian directly to the owner, followed by a service invoice under the agreement. Do not redirect recoveries into the operator's account simply to improve collection speed. Document fee collection rights, permitted payment mechanics, and dispute handling in advance. If a claimant will not use secure intake, offer custodian-direct document submission instead of accepting identity images through casual messaging.

sections.heading: 3. Convert Evidence into Conversations with a Restrained Multi-Channel System
paragraphs: Run outbound as a verification offer, not a windfall announcement. On day one, send a short business email or sealed letter identifying the operator, the official custodian, the historical entity or address match, and the owner's ability to claim directly without hiring a service. Avoid displaying full property details on postcards or voicemail. State the service plainly: ownership research, document coordination, submission support, and status tracking where permitted. On day four, place one manual call to an independently sourced business number; ask who handles legacy receivables rather than requesting identity documents. On day ten, send an evidence-led follow-up with an official portal link and a redacted example of the document checklist. On day twenty-one, close the sequence with a clear opt-out and pause further prospecting unless the recipient reengages. Honor rejection immediately across every channel. Apply CAN-SPAM requirements to commercial email, including accurate headers, a postal address, and a functioning opt-out. Assess TCPA and applicable state restrictions before calling or texting; do not assume a public number authorizes automated outreach. Treat this cadence as a testable operating hypothesis, not permission to contact every listed owner repeatedly. Track replies by source and representative role.

Build inbound around questions that reveal document friction: 'claiming property after a merger,' 'old company address on a treasury record,' and 'estate claim representative documents.' Publish jurisdiction-specific checklists that link to the official agency and distinguish free owner claiming from paid coordination. Avoid pages that imitate treasury branding or imply government affiliation. A useful page names the ownership problem, lists the records usually requested, explains what varies by custodian, and offers a short eligibility conversation without requesting sensitive identifiers. Use Search Console to identify relevant queries and a simple CRM source field to connect inquiries with signed and collected cases. Public search demand is a sourcing signal, not evidence that any particular visitor owns property. Develop referral relationships with bookkeepers, corporate secretaries, probate practitioners, and business wind-down specialists who encounter missing-record problems. Give each partner a one-page referral checklist and a secure introduction process. Disclose and verify any referral compensation before offering it, particularly where professional conduct rules or finder-fee restrictions apply. Start with unpaid reciprocal education rather than assuming a referral commission is permissible. One controller introduction covering five related entities can produce better-qualified work than hundreds of anonymous impressions.

Handle objections by reducing information asymmetry rather than increasing pressure. When an owner asks whether this is a scam, provide the official portal, business identity, written scope, and an independently verifiable contact route; never ask them to trust a screenshot alone. When they ask why they should pay, explain the specific historical records and coordination tasks involved, then acknowledge that uncomplicated claims may be better handled directly. When they say the money is theirs, agree: the engagement purchases administrative work, not ownership of their asset. When a controller already has a recovery vendor, ask whether an uncovered entity or jurisdiction exists without requesting another provider's confidential files. Quote fees only after checking the property and contract rules. Avoid artificial deadlines, guaranteed payout dates, or claims that the owner will lose money merely by declining. End the conversation with one concrete next step: confirm the representative, review a redacted checklist, or receive the direct-claim link. Record objection categories so the weekly review can distinguish distrust, weak economics, unavailable documents, and timing restrictions. Each category demands a different correction; rewriting subject lines cannot fix an ineligible agreement or an inaccessible ownership archive.

sections.heading: 4. Engineer the First Three-to-Ten Wins and Reconcile the Annual Cases
paragraphs: Define a win as an owner-paid recovery with the operator's contractual fee collected; track signed mandates separately. For an initial planning cohort, start with 500 raw records, deduplicate and qualify 200, reach 80 verified decision-makers, hold 24 substantive conversations, sign 12 mandates, complete nine claim packets, and target six paid wins within the 3–12 month planning window. These are illustrative test assumptions, not observed conversion benchmarks or agency processing commitments. They imply 40% raw-to-qualified, 40% qualified-to-reached, 30% reached-to-conversation, 50% conversation-to-mandate, 75% mandate-to-complete, and approximately 67% complete-to-paid conversion. Overall raw-to-paid conversion is 1.2%. At that assumed yield, three wins require approximately 250 raw records and ten require approximately 834. Do not extrapolate until a matured cohort supports the rates. A recent submission awaiting review is different from a rejected claim; report aged cohorts and unresolved cases explicitly. Separate state, property category, referral source, and representative type so one unusually easy corporate cluster does not inflate every channel forecast. If conversations are strong but packet completion is weak, improve evidence intake before adding leads. If packets are complete but payments lag, investigate custodian requests and realistic cash timing rather than intensifying outbound.

Reconcile the annual economics to recognized service fees, never to the owner's recovered principal. One illustrative Conservative bridge is 30 completed engagements averaging $2,000 in recognized fees: $60,000 revenue, $45,000 operating costs, and $15,000 owner net profit at 25%, staffed by 1 FT + 2 C. The Base bridge is 51 engagements averaging $5,000: $255,000 revenue, $159,375 costs, and $95,625 profit at 37.5%, also 1 FT + 2 C. Scaled is 75 engagements averaging $6,000: $450,000 revenue, $225,000 costs, and $225,000 profit at 50%, staffed by 2 FT + 3 C. These engagement counts explain the fixed scorecard; they are not additional performance promises. At a uniformly allowable 10% fee, the implied recovered principal would be $600,000, $2,550,000, and $4,500,000 respectively. Different lawful rates change principal requirements, not the canonical fee totals. Keep the medical adjacency outside this bridge unless a separately reconciled operating plan replaces the illustrative engagement mix. The first six wins at $2,000 each produce $12,000 of fees, not the Conservative annual target. Maintain separate dates for owner payment, operator collection, and accounting recognition under the adopted revenue policy.

Sequence execution around working capital and case maturity. In month one, establish the jurisdiction rules sheet, secure intake, a fifty-record research batch, and two professional referral conversations. During months two and three, run weekly batches, test the outreach sequence, and submit only complete authorized files. During months four through twelve, service custodian requests, invoice earned fees, and expand only the source cohorts with demonstrated contribution. The canonical startup capital range is $5,000–$35,000; its $1,500–$8,000 monthly opex range is a planning envelope, not a ceiling on all annual case-related costs. The Base and Scaled total cost budgets exceed that range when annualized, so explicitly bridge fixed overhead, contractor processing, acquisition work, and other variable costs rather than hiding the difference. A founder can handle owner relationships while contractors research records and assemble packets, with access limited by task. Add the second full-time role only when collected contribution and documented backlog support it. Automate record matching suggestions and claim-status reminders first; require human review for identity collisions, authority changes, and fee exceptions. Close each month by reconciling the CRM, custodian correspondence, invoices, and bank receipts. Expand the machine only when those four records tell the same story.

sections.heading: 1. Convert twelve recovery routes into evidence-backed production lanes
paragraphs: Start with the administering treasury, not a purchased list promising instant recoveries. Download permitted state search results or holder records, preserve the retrieval date and source locator, and assign one internal case to each jurisdiction/property identifier. A name match is a lead, never proof of ownership. The twelve routes below are this chapter's operational mapping, not twelve independent revenue forecasts: eleven address recovery evidence patterns and one addresses an adjacent tax-appeal service. California Code of Civil Procedure sections 1540 and 1582 illustrate why claim authority and finder compensation must be checked separately. Record the applicable agreement restrictions, fee ceiling, waiting interval, registration requirements, and version date before outreach progresses into engagement. Explain that the owner can claim directly through the administering agency without hiring the service. Offer a plain description of the work purchased: locating records, resolving discrepancies, assembling evidence, and tracking requests. Never imply treasury affiliation. For the Base illustration, a successful case releases $12,500 to its owner and earns a separately collectible $1,250 service fee where that ten-percent arrangement is permitted. That distinction follows the case through every screen.

Build evidence requirements around the ownership chain rather than one universal upload form. An individual may need a former-address connection; a renamed company may need amendments and merger documents; an estate may require current appointment papers and the agency's specific claimant process. Corporate uncashed warrants require an additional question: is the item still payable by the issuing agency, already transferred to a treasury, or subject to a separate reissue procedure? A stale payment image alone does not settle that question. Use the official corporate registry, county recorder, issuing controller, and treasury claim portal as distinct sources. Store sensitive documents in an encrypted document repository with individual access grants; the ledger stores opaque evidence references rather than identity-document contents. Ask only for documents needed for the particular claim, and remove rejected prospect documents under a documented retention schedule. Escalate competing heirs, conflicting corporate successors, and uncertain signatures instead of converting a matching score into authorization. The economic stop is equally concrete: a $300 property at ten percent yields $30 before labor, so direct the owner to self-service unless lawful aggregation makes the work economical.

The mapped adjacent play property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency begins when the county releases annual assessment notices and valuation rolls. Ingest parcel identifiers, assessed values, building characteristics, exemptions, and comparable sales or neighborhood equity ratios. An automated valuation model flags apparent overassessment; a qualified reviewer checks comparability, valuation date, jurisdictional appeal grounds, and filing authority before any protest. A $500,000 assessment reduction at an illustrative two-percent effective tax rate produces $10,000 of first-year tax reduction. A lawful contract charging thirty to fifty percent of the verified reduction produces $3,000 to $5,000 in fees; a $1,000 local representation cost leaves $2,000 to $4,000 before other expenses. Keep those fees outside the unclaimed-property scorecard and outside the cohort below. Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1152 supplies a concrete registration screen, while Texas Tax Code section 41.44 supplies protest deadlines that must be calculated from the actual notice and applicable exception. The fallback is a licensed local consultant or attorney of record where required, using reviewed pre-deadline batch electronic filings only where the county supports them. A missed deadline or weak comparable set cancels that parcel's production slot.

sections.heading: 2. Install the six-module ledger and make every local write replay-safe
paragraphs: The six modules form one copy-pasteable Python reference program: concatenate their code cells in order and run them with Python 3.9 or later. They use only SQLite and the standard library, create a local recovery.sqlite3 file, and expose functions rather than initiating treasury requests. Execute them first against a disposable database; this chapter supplies reference source, not a report of executed tests. The design assumes one trusted application service owns database writes, local storage implements SQLite locking correctly, and each worker opens its own connection. Do not place the live database on an ordinary network filesystem. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes writers before they inspect state; unique property keys, unique receipt references, and immutable accounting rows provide additional barriers. A busy timeout produces an explicit failure rather than permission to skip locking. Each operation stores a canonical request fingerprint and response inside the same transaction as its changes. Repeating the same operation returns its recorded result; reusing its key with different input fails. These mechanisms remove check-then-write races within this local ledger under the stated deployment boundaries.

Keep the state machine narrower than the marketing funnel. INTAKE becomes VERIFIED only after identity, authority, current jurisdiction rules, and a permitted agreement have been checked outside the scoring function. FILED requires an official submission reference, APPROVED requires agency evidence, and OWNER_PAID requires evidence that the owner actually received the property. The reference stores that evidence's opaque identifier and writes a permanent transition record. ESCROW_REVIEW is an exception state, not an escrow account: the business does not receive, pool, or redistribute client principal. Its only exit returns to VERIFIED after documented resolution, requiring later filing stages to be established again. If a matter genuinely requires custody or escrow, route it to a separately authorized provider and keep it out of this payment workflow. The scoring script ranks expected effort using nonnegative integer cents and evidence indicators; it cannot establish ownership or waive a statutory restriction. Reject oversized integers, empty identifiers, and contradictory duplicate property records before they enter the working queue. A low score influences priority, not the legal validity of someone's claim.

Invoice creation is permitted only after OWNER_PAID, using the fee frozen at intake and confirmed during verification. That recognition rule assumes a contract whose recovery service is earned at this documented event; contracts with materially different performance terms need a separately reviewed accounting rule. Database triggers create the receivable/revenue posting and move the case to INVOICED atomically. A full bank receipt creates the bank/receivable posting and moves it to SETTLED. Each journal row contains one equal debit-credit pair, so the reference cannot create an internally unbalanced posting. Invoice and receipt tables are immutable, and their unique constraints prevent a second invoice or settlement for the same case. The intentionally narrow model accepts one full fee payment, not partial payments, refunds, credit notes, write-offs, or multi-invoice remittances. Route those exceptions to a separately designed accounting workflow rather than editing history. Use posted bank references, not emailed payment screenshots. Processor fees are separate expenses, never an unexplained reduction of recognized fees or an excuse to mark a short receipt as full settlement.

Reconciliation is a three-way comparison: the signed fee schedule and owner distribution evidence support the invoice; the invoice supports the journal; the posted bank transaction supports the receipt. The view reports fee revenue, bank collections, and outstanding receivables by claim, while the QA module checks referential integrity, amount consistency, and accounting state. Those checks cannot authenticate a forged document or prove that a bank reference was independently reviewed. Keep reviewer identity and source evidence in the protected case system, and resolve every exception before reporting collectible cash. Treasury portals also sit outside the database transaction. Without a documented agency idempotency mechanism, exactly-once external submission cannot be promised: use one designated submitter per case, preserve submission receipts, and investigate an uncertain response before retrying. Never automatically repeat a filing because a browser timed out. Test parallel duplicate intake, repeated receipt delivery, conflicting operation payloads, and interrupted commits in an isolated environment before deployment. The reference ledger covers service-fee receivables and receipts; payroll, contractor costs, taxes, and financing remain in the operator's complete accounting system.

Module 5 — claim-level revenue, bank, and receivable reconciliation view

db.executescript('''
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS fee_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    c.claim_id,
    c.jurisdiction,
    c.property_key,
    c.state,
    i.invoice_id,
    COALESCE(i.amount_cents, 0) AS invoice_cents,
    COALESCE(r.amount_cents, 0) AS receipt_cents,
    COALESCE(j.revenue_cents, 0) AS revenue_cents,
    COALESCE(j.bank_cents, 0) AS bank_cents,
    COALESCE(j.receivable_cents, 0) AS receivable_cents
FROM claims c
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.claim_id = c.claim_id
LEFT JOIN receipts r ON r.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        invoice_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN credit_account = 'fee_revenue'
                 THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents,
        SUM(CASE WHEN debit_account = 'bank'
                 THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS bank_cents,
        SUM(CASE
            WHEN debit_account = 'receivable' THEN amount_cents
            WHEN credit_account = 'receivable' THEN -amount_cents
            ELSE 0 END) AS receivable_cents
    FROM journal
    GROUP BY invoice_id
) j ON j.invoice_id = i.invoice_id;
''')

def reconciliation_rows():
    return [
        dict(row) for row in db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM fee_reconciliation ORDER BY claim_id"
        )
    ]
Compare this service-fee subledger with bank statements and the complete operating ledger before closing each month.
Module 6 — snapshot-consistent structural and accounting QA checks

def quality_checks():
    db.execute("BEGIN")
    try:
        integrity = db.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchall()
        if [row[0] for row in integrity] != ["ok"]:
            raise RuntimeError("SQLite integrity check failed")
        if db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall():
            raise RuntimeError("Foreign-key check failed")
        failures = db.execute('''
            SELECT claim_id FROM fee_reconciliation
            WHERE revenue_cents != invoice_cents
               OR bank_cents != receipt_cents
               OR receivable_cents != invoice_cents - receipt_cents
               OR receivable_cents < 0
               OR (state = 'SETTLED' AND (
                   invoice_cents = 0 OR receipt_cents != invoice_cents
               ))
               OR (state = 'INVOICED' AND (
                   invoice_cents = 0 OR receipt_cents != 0
               ))
               OR (invoice_cents > 0 AND state NOT IN ('INVOICED', 'SETTLED'))
        ''').fetchall()
        if failures:
            raise RuntimeError("Claim accounting reconciliation failed")
        missing_operations = db.execute('''
            SELECT t.transition_id
            FROM transitions t
            LEFT JOIN operations o ON o.operation_key = t.operation_key
            WHERE o.operation_key IS NULL
        ''').fetchall()
        if missing_operations:
            raise RuntimeError("Transition operation evidence is incomplete")
        totals = dict(db.execute('''
            SELECT
                COALESCE(SUM(revenue_cents), 0) AS revenue_cents,
                COALESCE(SUM(bank_cents), 0) AS bank_cents,
                COALESCE(SUM(receivable_cents), 0) AS receivable_cents
            FROM fee_reconciliation
        ''').fetchone())
        db.execute("COMMIT")
        return totals
    except BaseException:
        if db.in_transaction:
            db.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
Run read-only checks against a consistent snapshot, then separately verify evidence authenticity and duplicate-delivery behavior.

sections.heading: 3. Run intake, submission, collection, and close as four accountable handoffs
paragraphs: Assign the Base team as one full-time operator plus two contractors, not three interchangeable generalists. The operator owns client relationships, jurisdiction decisions, exception disposition, and monthly close. One contractor normalizes public records and assembles evidence requests; the other reviews packet completeness and monitors agency correspondence under limited access. Neither contractor needs unrestricted identity-document exports or authority to change payout instructions. In a sixty-lead monthly cohort, remove twelve duplicate or previously resolved records, eighteen identity or authority mismatches, and ten cases whose lawful fee cannot support production cost. That leaves twenty qualified files. Reserve three further losses for withdrawals, agency denials, or unresolved evidence, producing seventeen eventual paid fees in the illustration. These are mutually exclusive outcome buckets, not overlapping rejection percentages. Record the actual reason and date for each exit so acquisition quality can be measured by source and claimant type. Avoid replacing a missing document with an optimistic probability. A queue should contain a next action, named responsible role, and evidence deadline; otherwise its aging report merely counts neglected cases rather than controllable work.

After engagement, assemble one versioned packet manifest showing each requested document, repository reference, reviewer, and official submission identifier. Check the current treasury instructions immediately before filing because forms and acceptable evidence can change between prospecting and submission. Use the agency's secure upload method where offered; keep passwords, authentication codes, and complete identity numbers out of shared task notes. Status tracking can poll a permitted API or generate reminders for manual portal review, but it should not bypass access controls or treat a missing response as a denial. Set internal follow-up intervals from the agency's published process and the case's last substantive event, not from an invented universal payment deadline. Record each request for additional evidence as a separate task tied to the original claim. Before responding, verify that the requesting message actually comes from the agency. A changed beneficiary, substituted bank account, or request to route principal through the recovery business triggers an exception review. Filing volume is a throughput metric; it is not recognized revenue and cannot fund payroll before collections arrive.

Close the loop only after independently supporting both the owner's recovery and the operator's receipt. The owner distribution record establishes the contractual fee event in this model; the bank credit establishes cash. If the owner has recovered property but has not paid the fee, show a receivable and a collection task rather than deleting the invoice or reporting settlement. Reconcile contract amount, invoice, bank reference, and journal totals at least monthly, with a second reviewer checking exceptions and changes to payment instructions. Distinguish fixed operating overhead from variable delivery costs when comparing economics with the scorecard. The Base walk uses $6,000 monthly fixed overhead, within the stated $1,500–$8,000 monthly operating range, plus $7,281.25 of variable case-delivery and collection costs. Total modeled monthly expense is $13,281.25. The fixed bucket includes modeled operator compensation and platform overhead; contractor effort and other delivery charges belong in the variable bucket without double counting. Owner net profit is the residual after those modeled expenses. Maintain invoice-level support for the cost categories rather than presenting this illustrative allocation as a quoted vendor budget.

sections.heading: 4. Walk a seasoned 90-day cohort without borrowing revenue from the future
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk is a steady-state illustration, not a day-one startup forecast. Assume January through March constitute the measurement window and that October, November, and December intake cohorts already exist at opening. Each older cohort contains sixty original leads with the same eventual disposition: twelve duplicates, eighteen mismatches, ten uneconomic cases, three later losses, and seventeen successful fee cases. The older cohorts mature one per month during the window. January, February, and March intake repeats the sixty-lead process, but their seventeen eventual successes are planning estimates, not booked receivables. For illustration they mature in April, May, and June respectively; actual treasury timing can be longer. This respects the volume's three-to-twelve-month time to first deal rather than promising collections during the first ninety days of a new business. Opening operating cash is $35,000 after any earlier setup spending, funded before the illustrated window. That reserve is not revenue, and it should not be confused with a claim that all prior startup costs and three months of operations fit inside the same amount.

Each maturing cohort produces seventeen owner distributions of $12,500, or $212,500 of client property, and seventeen $1,250 fees, or $21,250 of recognized operator revenue. Assume owners receive their property and pay their full fees within the same measurement month; ending fee receivables are therefore zero in this particular walk. Monthly fixed overhead of $6,000 plus variable costs of $7,281.25 produces $13,281.25 of total expense and $7,968.75 of owner net profit. Cumulative operating cash contribution is $7,968.75 after January, $15,937.50 after February, and $23,906.25 after March. Adding the opening reserve gives closing cash of $42,968.75, $50,937.50, and $58,906.25. These balances assume no owner distributions, debt service, new capital spending, or additional financing during the window, and modeled expenses are paid in their respective months. The table records new intake and old-cohort settlement separately so the same seventeen successes cannot be counted twice. The three later losses per cohort earn no fee, and their pursuit cost is already inside the modeled operating expense rather than silently omitted from margin.

Across ninety days, recognized fees total $63,750, operating expense totals $39,843.75, and owner net profit totals $23,906.25. Multiplying those steady-state quarterly figures by four produces exactly $255,000 revenue, $159,375 expense, and $95,625 owner net profit: the canonical 37.5-percent Base margin. Underlying client recoveries total $637,500 during the quarter and $2,550,000 at the illustrated annual cadence, but neither figure belongs in operator revenue. The other scorecard cases remain separate: Conservative revenue of $60,000 less $45,000 expense yields $15,000 profit at twenty-five percent; Scaled revenue of $450,000 less $225,000 expense yields $225,000 profit at fifty percent. Do not transplant Base lead conversion into those cases without a new capacity model. Stress the cash walk by delaying one month's fee receipts: $21,250 moves from bank cash into receivables if recovery and earning conditions are already satisfied. If the owner distribution itself is delayed, fee recognition also moves. Continue paying actual delivery costs, reforecast runway weekly, and reduce discretionary acquisition before relying on uncertain treasury payments to cover committed expenses.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #5, Unclaimed Property Recovery, holds Rank #04 with an 89/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its information advantage comes from connecting treasury property records to defensible ownership evidence, not buying larger contact lists. This chapter organizes 12 mapped plays: eleven chapter-local recovery workflows and the specified transferable-tax-credit adjacency. An eighteen-source directory separates searchable portals from documented APIs, while operating matrices translate matches into authorized claims, controlled enrichment spend, and auditable fee collections. The canonical annual owner-profit cases remain $15,000 Conservative, $95,625 Base, and $225,000 Scaled; recovered client assets never become desk revenue. Build around source provenance, identity resolution, claim-status tracking, state-specific finder rules, and direct-claim disclosure. Treat tax-credit origination as a separately qualified workflow with direct eligible transfers and buyer-funded escrow, not speculative credit inventory.

sections.heading: 1. Build an eighteen-source directory around custody, ownership, and permitted access
paragraphs: Start with the custodian, not the enrichment vendor. State treasury systems establish that a property record exists; they do not establish that your prospect owns it, that the displayed amount is complete, or that a finder may charge immediately. Create one source register with jurisdiction, official landing URL, documented access method, retrieval timestamp, publication date when available, and the current finder rule reference. MissingMoney provides useful participating-state discovery, while California, Texas, Florida, and New York supply jurisdiction-specific search and claim instructions. Coverage differs, so a missing aggregator result never closes a lead. Corporate uncashed warrants need an additional classification: some remain with the issuing agency before eventual treasury custody. Record the warrant issuer, issue date, stale-date procedure, and replacement route before calling the item escheated property. The directory below gives operating check intervals rather than promising publisher refresh schedules. Check terms and current official links at onboarding, because portal vendors and export permissions change. A browser search box is not permission to replay private endpoints or bypass interactive access controls. Prefer an agency-approved extract when recurring manual search becomes the bottleneck.

Use entity evidence to turn an attractive name into a defensible claimant chain. SEC submissions identify registrants and filing histories; secretary-of-state records establish entity status and filed name changes; merger documents connect predecessor names to surviving corporations. None independently proves entitlement to a particular treasury item. A dissolved company may require a winding-up representative, and an asset purchase may exclude cash receivables that a stock acquisition would leave inside the same legal entity. Retrieve the operative document rather than inferring succession from matching websites. For an estate, use the relevant county court's authorized records channel and obtain the appointment instrument needed by the custodian; a death notice does not appoint a representative. For a warrant, confirm the payee's original legal identity with the issuing agency before building a treasury claim. Store public business evidence separately from owner identity documents, with narrower access for the latter. PACER, county clerks, and state filing offices are fallback evidence sources, not universal entitlement APIs. Measure evidence completeness by missing required instruments, not by the number of commercial databases queried during research.

The directory deliberately mixes official sources, commercial APIs, and diagnostic tools without pretending they have equivalent authority. OpenCorporates can accelerate entity discovery, Melissa can normalize an address, and Twilio Lookup can describe a telephone number; none proves ownership or permission to contact. Use commercial results as leads back to authoritative records. For sources without published quotas, choose low-volume manual research or obtain a written extract arrangement instead of inventing a safe requests-per-second number. For documented APIs, record the account quota, identify the client where required, cache stable responses, and honor throttling responses. Cost entries distinguish free public search from paid copies and contracted usage; procurement must capture current prices before activation. The eleven recovery mappings in this chapter are local operating labels: treasury discovery, warrant tracing, predecessor resolution, merger succession, estate authority, address normalization, contact verification, property deduplication, claim packaging, status monitoring, and fee reconciliation. The twelfth mapping is the specified transferable-credit adjacency. This distinction keeps an incomplete cross-volume roster from becoming invented candidate metadata while still giving the desk twelve concrete workflows to instrument and evaluate.

sections.heading: 2. Turn discovery into a provenance-preserving enrichment waterfall
paragraphs: Build the ingestion layer with Python's urllib.request, csv, json, sqlite3, hashlib, and datetime before purchasing an orchestration platform. Use only documented API or export access authorized for the source; browser-only portals stay in a manual research queue. Preserve each permitted source artifact with retrieval time, original URL, content hash, parser version, and source publication date when supplied. A hash supports change detection and integrity checks, not confidentiality. Keep raw artifacts separate from normalized records so a parser correction can be replayed without silently rewriting evidence. Normalize business suffixes, punctuation, whitespace, and address components into comparison fields while retaining the original strings. Use the custodian's property identifier as the primary deduplication anchor when available; otherwise build a composite candidate key and flag collisions for review. Two records sharing a name and amount can still represent different properties. A disappearing search result is not proof of payment. Represent it as a source observation requiring confirmation. SQLite transactions should commit artifact metadata and normalized records together, preventing an apparently complete lead from pointing to evidence that was never actually saved.

Run enrichment in a strict waterfall: property existence, entity identity, historical address, successor authority, claimant contact, then document collection. Spend on the next stage only when the prior stage supports a plausible claim. Illustratively, reviewing 200 records at three minutes each requires ten hours; at a $35 loaded hourly rate, discovery costs $350. If twenty records survive, assign a $0.25 budget ceiling per initial commercial address check, adding $5 rather than enriching all 200. Those are internal planning assumptions, not quoted vendor prices. If five prospects then require twenty minutes of authority review, another $58.33 brings cohort research cost to $413.33 before outreach and claim preparation. Stop when expected collectible fees cannot cover the remaining workload. Matching scores must expose evidence: exact historical address, documented predecessor name, official entity identifier, and corroborated representative authority. A common surname plus a nearby city should never trigger automatic claimant selection. Route conflicting names, competing successors, estate disputes, and multiple plausible owners into an exception queue. The fallback is a direct custodian inquiry or additional owner evidence, not more aggressive personal-data collection from unrelated commercial sources.

Keep sensitive claimant documents out of enrichment payloads and ordinary CRM notes. Store identification, tax identifiers, estate instruments, and bank instructions in a restricted document repository with access logs and a defined retention schedule. Contractors receive only the records needed for their assigned review; the owner handles disputed authority and payment instructions. Public availability does not erase contractual restrictions or make every personal-data product suitable for this purpose. Do not obtain consumer reports without a qualifying purpose under 15 U.S.C. § 1681b, or motor-vehicle personal information outside 18 U.S.C. § 2721's permitted-use framework. Prefer business filings and claimant-supplied evidence. Outreach should identify the recovery business, explain the specific property lead without exposing unnecessary personal details, disclose the owner's ability to claim directly, and state the proposed fee basis. A commercial phone lookup is neither contact permission nor proof that the person answering owns the asset. Maintain suppression requests across vendors and campaigns. Measure false matches, unresolved authority conflicts, document rework, and accepted claims by source. Those diagnostics reveal whether the waterfall is improving decision quality rather than merely producing more completed database fields.
